findings.first_evidence: lib/live/provider-costs.ts:149 --     if (began > cutoff || (ended !== null && (ended < began || ended > cutoff))) throw new Error('Ledger timestamps contradict its observation cutoff');
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the impossible-timestamp guards for startedAt after cutoff and endedAt before startedAt, but accommodate closure after cutoff: exclude sessions starting at or beyond period.end before that check, and treat endedAt after cutoff as an open/boundary session at the cutoff instead of rejecting the entire export. Add a regression using buildCostReport output where an unrelated session closes one second after cutoff while comparing the previous UTC day.
findings.title: Concurrent session closure blocks historical cost comparisons
findings.why_it_matters: A normal unfiltered voice-costs export can prevent any historical comparison when a session closes during the export. The exporter fixes cutoff before its asynchronous reads, filters sessions only by created_at, and copies their current ended_at; the new importer rejects endedAt after cutoff before excluding unrelated dates. Treating these sessions as still open at cutoff, and excluding sessions starting outside the selected window first, preserves conservative accounting without making unrelated live activity invalidate the entire report.
findings.validation_reason: When a session created before the export cutoff closes between cutoff capture and the session query, scripts/voice-costs.ts:19,26,64-66 and lib/live/cost-report.ts:98,212 emit its later endedAt, which the newly added lib/live/provider-costs.ts:149 rejects before excluding unrelated periods at line 150; a read-only Node v23.3.0 reproduction using costRow/buildCostReport confirmed that a session closing one second after cutoff blocks the previous UTC day's comparison while the same still-open session is excluded successfully, although production incidence was not measured.
